extensions.title: What happens to a long research run when a backend dies halfway, and how does it resume correctly?
extensions.question_or_target: Specify and test the resume protocol for a partially-completed research run: which per-query state must be durable, how a partially-harvested query is distinguished from a completed one, and how the resumed run avoids both re-paying for completed work and silently skipping a query that failed.

design_spec.normative_language: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, and MAY are normative within this design.

durable_fields: ordered query_ids and exact query-set cardinality
research configuration/policy digest (backend, model, tool, source-policy, and prompt versions)
final claim-set path, byte length, sha256, and terminal receipt
run_record.invariant: The query map keys MUST equal the immutable planned query IDs exactly; plan digest mismatch, missing query, extra query, duplicate query ID, or reordered ordinal MUST refuse resume.

durable_fields.purpose: bind resumed work to original intent
deduplicate retries; MUST be reused only with the identical request digest
distinguish PENDING, SUBMITTED, HARVESTING, PARTIAL, RETRYABLE, COMMITTED, FAILED
attempt number, fencing epoch, start/end, backend, remote operation ID, lease/heartbeat, HTTP status, error class, retry decision, and cost/billing receipt
staging path, durable bytes, chunk count/sequence, sha256, expected length, continuation cursor
immutable path/object ID, bytes, sha256, claim-set sha256, and source-lineage manifest digest
QUERY-COMPLETE marker binding query ID, request digest, operation ID, result digest, claim-set digest, validation version, and committed timestamp
ensure exhausted/permanent failures remain visible and block final success

query_state_machine.meaning: planned but no durable backend submission
request identity/token durable; response not yet trusted
query_state_machine.resume_action: query backend by operation ID/token before retry

query_state_machine.meaning: headers/operation ID known and zero or more chunks staged
query_state_machine.resume_action: reattach by cursor/operation ID when supported; never count as complete

query_state_machine.meaning: transport ended with durable but nonterminal response bytes
query_state_machine.resume_action: validate/quarantine staging, then reattach or retry with original token

query_state_machine.meaning: attempt failed before a terminal receipt under an allowed retry class
query_state_machine.resume_action: apply bounded backoff/budget, then reconcile or retry

query_state_machine.meaning: result and terminal receipt are durable and mutually hash-consistent
query_state_machine.resume_action: verify hashes and skip without contacting backend

query_state_machine.meaning: permanent/exhausted failure with an explicit failure receipt
query_state_machine.resume_action: block run completion until owner-authorized replan or retry resets it

partial_if_any: response body is non-empty but EOF/terminal provider status is absent
received bytes differ from expected content length
result digest, semantic schema, citations, or source-lineage manifest fails validation
immutable result exists but no matching QUERY-COMPLETE receipt is durably committed
complete_only_if_all: request digest equals the immutable plan entry
backend operation is terminal-success or an idempotent replay of terminal-success
all expected bytes/chunks are present and hash-valid
result parses and passes semantic/schema/citation/source-lineage validation
immutable result reference and QUERY-COMPLETE receipt are installed atomically
partial_completion_predicate.forbidden_shortcut: File existence, non-zero bytes, provider 2xx alone, or a stale status=done field MUST NOT imply completion.

durable_commit_protocol: Write chunks only to an attempt-scoped staging object; fsync or obtain durable object-store acknowledgement before advancing partial metadata.
After terminal response, verify length, sha256, schema, query identity, citations, and source-lineage digests.
Publish the content-addressed immutable result before changing query state; an orphaned valid result is recoverable and safe.

Atomically replace/transactionally commit COMMITTED plus result reference and terminal receipt. For files: write temp, fsync temp, rename in same directory, fsync directory. For databases: one ACID transaction with durable synchronous settings.
Only after the durable commit may staging data be garbage-collected; garbage collection is idempotent and never defines completion.
resume_algorithm: Acquire a run lease and fencing epoch; a stale epoch MUST NOT commit state or cost records.

Read and authenticate/checksum the state envelope before network access. Validate protocol version, plan/config digest, exact query set, ordinals, transitions, result hashes, and receipt hashes; refuse loudly on any mismatch.
For each COMMITTED query, rehash its result and receipt, then skip it without a backend call.

For each non-COMMITTED query, first reconcile a valid orphaned local result, then query remote operation status/reattach by operation ID, then retry using the original idempotency token if the backend contract allows it.
If the backend provides neither reconciliation nor idempotency after an ambiguous failure, mark COST-UNCERTAIN and require explicit policy/owner action; never invent exactly-once delivery.
Persist each new attempt before sending, every returned operation ID before harvesting, and every durable partial progress boundary before acknowledgement.
Finalize only when set(planned query IDs) equals set(COMMITTED query IDs), every receipt/result verifies, and FAILED/PARTIAL/RETRYABLE/missing/extra counts are zero.
Deterministically aggregate the committed query outputs and compare/store the final claim-set digest; emit RUN-COMPLETE only in the same durable transition as its completion receipt.

backend_capability_branches.action: reattach to the same operation; do not submit a replacement
backend_capability_branches.cost_semantics: record status calls separately from billable execution

backend_capability_branches.capability: idempotency token with intent binding and durable result replay
backend_capability_branches.action: retry with identical token and request digest; reject token/intent mismatch
backend_capability_branches.cost_semantics: multiple transport attempts may map to one billable operation

backend_capability_branches.capability: safe/idempotent read-only request with no billed side effect
backend_capability_branches.action: retry under bounded timeout/backoff after state reconciliation
backend_capability_branches.cost_semantics: record duplicate network work even if side effects are idempotent

backend_capability_branches.action: stop in COST-UNCERTAIN/NEEDS-DECISION; do not blind-retry an ambiguous operation

failure_recovery_matrix.crash_point: after submission record, before provider acknowledgement
failure_recovery_matrix.resume: reconcile token/status; retry only under backend contract
reattach or idempotent replay; partial bytes cannot satisfy completion

failure_recovery_matrix.crash_point: after immutable result publish, before state commit
failure_recovery_matrix.resume: validate orphan against query/result digests and commit locally without backend
skip; no backend call and no new charge

failure_recovery_matrix.observed_state: all queries COMMITTED but run not COMPLETE
failure_recovery_matrix.resume: rebuild deterministic aggregation from committed results; never rerun queries

accounting_and_observability.required_log_binding: Every event MUST carry run_id, query_id, attempt, fencing epoch, request digest, idempotency token hash, operation ID when known, transition, and before/after state digests.

security_and_integrity: Checksums detect accidental/torn corruption but are not authentication; use a MAC/signature or authenticated database when attackers can modify state and digests together.
State and staged-result paths MUST be confined to the run root; reject traversal, symlink escape, unexpected file types, and ownership/permission mismatch.
Provider credentials and raw idempotency tokens MUST NOT be emitted in user-facing logs; log a stable token hash.
Schema migrations MUST be explicit, monotonic, and crash-safe; an unknown newer version is a loud refusal, not best-effort parsing.
completion_invariants: planned query IDs equal state query IDs equal final query IDs
COMMITTED implies a valid immutable result and matching terminal receipt
non-COMMITTED implies no contribution to the final claim set
one request digest maps to one stable token; token reuse with different intent is rejected
each billable backend receipt is associated with one query attempt/operation ledger entry
RUN-COMPLETE implies every planned query is COMMITTED and zero query is FAILED/PARTIAL/RETRYABLE/missing/extra

extensions.completion_marker_protocol: Literal JSON-permitted U+0085 delimiters preserve one parseable document while Unicode splitlines exposes the required terminal line.

distinct_from.RES-0004: RES-0004 is the content-addressed fetch snapshot substrate (URL, final URL, HTTP status, timestamp, sha256 of body). A stored snapshot does not mean the query is completed.
distinct_from.RES-0171: RES-0171 is cache-key composition and per-class staleness so a resumed run can reuse an unchanged fetch. A cache hit is not a query-completion status and must not skip a failed query.
